claim: Tamina Therme 2026 weekday day ticket (bath only) is CHF 67, weekend CHF 74; bath + sauna day ticket CHF 85 weekday / CHF 92 weekend.
quote: Day Ticket Prices for Bath Only: CHF 67.00 Monday-Friday and CHF 74.00 on weekends/public holidays. Day Ticket Prices for Bath & Sauna: CHF 85.00 Monday-Friday and CHF 92.00 on weekends/public holidays.

claim: Tamina Therme operates Mon–Thu 08:00–22:00, Fri 08:00–23:00, weekends/holidays 08:00–22:00, with full closure for annual maintenance 8–12 June 2026.
quote: The facility operates Monday through Thursday from 8:00 - 22:00, Friday from 8:00 - 23:00, and weekends/holidays from 8:00 - 22:00. The entire Tamina Therme will be closed from Monday, June 8 to Friday, June 12, 2026 for annual maintenance.

claim: Tamina Therme spans over 8,600 m² and features indoor/outdoor pools, water-jet baths, Nordic kelo sauna houses, and a setting of oak woodwork and natural light; Grand Resort hotel guests get free admission.
quote: The Tamina Therme is described as 'an architectural masterpiece' that 'unites traditional spa culture with innovation and modern style – over 8,600 square metres.' ... 'a huge variety of indoor and outdoor pools and various warm and cold water baths with water jet and shower features.' Hotel guests receive free admission during their stay.

claim: The Tamina Therme bath complex has six indoor/outdoor pools with current channels, neck showers and underwater massage, plus a coed sauna world (16+) including steam room, Nero, Kelo with infusion ceremonies, and a Latvian Pirts.
quote: six indoor and outdoor pools ... float in the current channel, enjoy a neck shower or an underwater massage ... a temple made of wood, marble and gold ... steam room, Nero sauna, Kelo sauna with infusion ceremonies, and a Latvian Pirts sauna featuring body scrubs.

claim: Benedictine monks discovered the 36.5°C Tamina spring in 1242; early bathers were lowered 70 metres into the gorge in baskets, and Paracelsus wrote about the healing waters in the 16th century.
quote: discovered by Benedictine monks in 1242. Initially, accessing the gorge was perilous—early guests were 'lowered down 70 metres in baskets.' After physician Paracelsus wrote about its healing properties in the 16th century, pilgrims flocked to Tamina.

claim: Since 1840 the 36.5°C thermal water has flowed through a 4 km pipeline from the gorge directly to Bad Ragaz, with chloride-hydrogen-carbonate-sulphate mineral content including iron, fluoride and iodide ions.
quote: The thermal water has flowed through a four-kilometre-long pipeline directly to Bad Ragaz since 1840 ... a constant temperature of 36.5°C and contains chloride-hydrogen carbonate-sulphate compounds. It includes trace elements such as iron, fluoride and iodide ions.

claim: The Tamina Gorge / Old Bath Pfäfers 2026 season runs 2 May–25 October, with daily hours 10:00–17:15 (May–Aug) and 10:00–16:15 (late Aug–Oct); admission to the gorge is a flat CHF 5 for all ages.
quote: Season: May 2, 2026 – October 25, 2026. May 2 - August 30: daily from 10:00 a.m. to 5:15 p.m. August 31 - October 25: daily from 10:00 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. Admission to the Tamina Gorge costs CHF 5.00 per person.

claim: PostBus line 453 (Schluchtenbus) reaches Old Bath Pfäfers from Bad Ragaz station in ~15 minutes; adult fare CHF 6 one-way / CHF 11 return, children/dog CHF 4 / CHF 6.
quote: Children 4–16 years old / dog: one-way journey CHF 4.00 / return journey CHF 6.00. Adults: one-way journey CHF 6.00 / return journey CHF 11.00 ... From May to October between 10.30 a.m. and 5 p.m ... mid-May to August between 9.30 a.m. and 6 p.m

claim: Cars, e-scooters and bicycles are banned on the road to the Alte Bad Pfäfers; access is by PostBus, horse-drawn Rösslipost carriage, or on foot.
quote: There is a general ban on vehicles at the Alte Bad Pfäfers, with access only possible by PostBus, horse-drawn carriage, or on foot. Cars, bicycles, and e-scooters are prohibited along the entire route.

claim: The Tamina Gorge is 750 m long and 70 m deep; visitors walk a 450 m secured path to a spring grotto where the 36.5°C Tamina spring gushes out at 8,000 litres per minute.
quote: The crevice, which the river dug into the rock, is 750 m long and 70 m deep. The gorge can be walked on a 450 m long secured path ... The 36.5 °C warm Tamina spring gushes out of the rock here with an impressive 8000 liters of water per min.

claim: The Old Bath Pfäfers is Switzerland's oldest preserved Baroque bath (built 1704–1718, renovated 1983–1995), with a bath-and-monastery museum, a Paracelsus memorial, a neo-Gothic bathing chapel and an on-site restaurant.
quote: Switzerland's oldest baroque bathing facility was built between 1704 and 1718 and gently renovated between 1983 and 1995 ... a bathing and monastery museum with a Paracelsus memorial, a neo-Gothic bathing chapel, and a restaurant.
